newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 110-125 bcf in wkly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 110-125 bcf in wkly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall 110-125 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 80 bcf to 165 bcf for the week ended Feb 14.

While the weather last week was mostly seasonal, traders on the high side of expectations expected mounting pressure to reduce stocks, particularly in the East where inventory levels were 261 bcf, or about 50 percent, above a year ago.
"It was a little cooler last week and people (eastern region utilities) have to start getting some gas out," said one East Coast trader.
In last report, overall stocks fell by just 60 bcf, well-below expectations, and were 212 bcf, or almost 20 percent, above last year. The four-week average drawdown is 158 bcf.
For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 93 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would cut the overall surplus to 1996 to about 185 bcf.
Eastern storage fell by 69 bcf last year, while producing stocks dropped by 21 bcf and western stocks by three bcf.
